x\displaystyle x :=ℒμBE​(π,r,f),M:=ℒ𝒟BE​(π,r,f),\displaystyle:=\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{BE}}(\pi,r,f),\qquad M:=\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathrm{BE}}(\pi,r,f),

we obtain

x≤M+2​εℱ,ℱ+163​β+8​β​x+43​β.\displaystyle x\leq M+2\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F},\mathcal{F}}+\frac{16}{3}\beta+\sqrt{8\beta x}+\frac{4}{3}\beta.

Using AM–GM, 8​β​x≤x/2+4​β\sqrt{8\beta x}\leq x/2+4\beta, so

x≤M+2​εℱ,ℱ+x2+4​β+163​β+43​β=M+2​εℱ,ℱ+x2+323​β,\displaystyle x\leq M+2\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F},\mathcal{F}}+\frac{x}{2}+4\beta+\frac{16}{3}\beta+\frac{4}{3}\beta=M+2\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F},\mathcal{F}}+\frac{x}{2}+\frac{32}{3}\beta,

and rearranging yields x≤2​M+4​εℱ,ℱ+643​βx\leq 2M+4\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F},\mathcal{F}}+\frac{64}{3}\beta. Equivalently,

ℒμBE​(π,r,f)≤2​ℒ𝒟BE​(π,r,f)+εBE+4​εℱ,ℱ,\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{BE}}(\pi,r,f)\leq 2\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathrm{BE}}(\pi,r,f)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{BE}}+4\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F},\mathcal{F}},

as claimed. ∎

B.3 Approximation and Comparator Lemmas

This subsection collects the approximation statements associated with the comparator pair (fπ,r⋆)(f_{\pi},r^{\star}) used in the pessimism step. We use the Bellman operator 𝒯r⋆π{\mathcal{T}}_{r^{\star}}^{\pi} from Eq. 1. The constants VmaxV_{\max} and εℱ\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F}} refer, respectively, to the uniform critic bound and the critic-realizability error in Assumption 2.

Lemma 12 (Adapted from Theorem 8 in Cheng et al. (2022)).

For any π∈Π\pi\in\Pi, let fπf_{\pi} be defined as follows,

fπ≔argminf∈ℱsuph,ν‖fh−(𝒯r⋆π​f)h‖2,ν2.\displaystyle f_{\pi}\coloneqq\mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{f\in\mathcal{F}}\sup_{h,\nu}\|f_{h}-({\mathcal{T}}_{r^{\star}}^{\pi}f)_{h}\|_{2,\nu}^{2}.

Under Assumptions 2 and 3, the following inequality holds with probability at least 1−δ1-\delta for all π∈Π\pi\in\Pi:

ℒ𝒟BE​(π,r⋆,fπ)≤εapx,εapx≔O⁡(H​Vmax2​log⁡(|ℱ|​|Π|/δ)n+εℱ).\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathrm{BE}}(\pi,r^{\star},f_{\pi})\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{apx}},\qquad\varepsilon_{\mathrm{apx}}\coloneqq O\bigg(\frac{HV^{2}_{\mathrm{max}}\log(|\mathcal{F}||\Pi|/\delta)}{n}+\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F}}\bigg).

The factor HH multiplying Vmax2V_{\max}^{2} in Lemma 12 comes from the sum-over-hh convention in Eq. 18: since rewards and critics are bounded (with Vmax=HV_{\max}=H in this section), each per-step squared residual is O⁡(Vmax2)O(V_{\max}^{2}), so one trajectory contributes O⁡(H​Vmax2)O(HV_{\max}^{2}). This is the finite-horizon analogue of the per-step residual bound in Cheng et al. (2022, Theorem 8); for infinite classes, the same argument uses covering numbers in place of |ℱ||\mathcal{F}| and |Π||\Pi|.

Lemma 13 (Finite-horizon performance difference lemma (Kakade and Langford, 2002)).

For any fixed per-step reward function rr and any policies π,π′∈Π\pi,\pi^{\prime}\in\Pi, let Jr​(π)≔𝔼τ∼π​[R⁡(τ,r)]J_{r}(\pi)\coloneqq\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\pi}[R(\tau;r)]. Then

Jr​(π)−Jr​(π′)=∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[Qhπ′,r​(sh,ah)−Vhπ′,r​(sh)].\displaystyle J_{r}(\pi)-J_{r}(\pi^{\prime})=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d_{h}^{\pi}}\bigl[Q_{h}^{\pi^{\prime},r}(s_{h},a_{h})-V_{h}^{\pi^{\prime},r}(s_{h})\bigr].

In particular, when r=r⋆r=r^{\star}, this reduces to the same identity under the shorthand notation introduced in Section 2.

Lemma 14 (Finite-horizon analogue of Eq. (16) in Cheng et al. (2022)).

Under Assumption 2, for every πk∈Π\pi_{k}\in\Pi,

|ℒμ​(πk,Qπk)−ℒμ​(πk,fπk)|≤2​H​εℱ=O⁡(H​εℱ).\displaystyle\bigl|\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},Q^{\pi_{k}})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},f_{\pi_{k}})\bigr|\leq 2H\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F}}}=O(H\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F}}}).
Proof.

Write f≔fπkf\coloneqq f_{\pi_{k}}, π≔πk\pi\coloneqq\pi_{k} and 𝒯π≔𝒯r⋆π{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}\coloneqq{\mathcal{T}}_{r^{\star}}^{\pi} throughout the proof. Define the fake per-step reward induced by (f,π)(f,\pi),

r~h(sh,ah)≔fh(sh,ah)−𝔼sh+1∼P(⋅∣sh,ah)[fh+1(sh+1,π(sh+1))],h∈[H],\displaystyle\widetilde{r}_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})\coloneqq f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-\mathbb{E}_{s_{h+1}\sim P(\cdot\mid s_{h},a_{h})}\bigl[f_{h+1}(s_{h+1},\pi(s_{h+1}))\bigr],\qquad h\in[H],

so that R⁡(τ,r~)=∑h=1Hr~h​(sh,ah)R(\tau;\widetilde{r})=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\widetilde{r}_{h}(s_{h},a_{h}), with fH+1≡0f_{H+1}\equiv 0. By construction ff satisfies the Bellman equation under reward r~\widetilde{r}, so fh=Qhπ,r~f_{h}=Q_{h}^{\pi,\widetilde{r}} and, letting Jr~​(⋅)J_{\widetilde{r}}(\cdot) denote the return in the MDP with reward r~\widetilde{r},

Jr~​(π)=f1​(s1,π),Jr~​(μ)=𝔼τ∼μ​[R⁡(τ,r~)].\displaystyle J_{\widetilde{r}}(\pi)=f_{1}(s_{1},\pi),\qquad J_{\widetilde{r}}(\mu)=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\mu}[R(\tau;\widetilde{r})]. (42)

Step 1: two applications of the performance difference lemma. By Lemma 13 applied in the true MDP,

ℒμ​(π,Qπ)=∑h=1H𝔼dhμ​[Vhπ​(sh)−Qhπ​(sh,ah)]=J⁡(π)−J⁡(μ).\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi,Q^{\pi})=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{d^{\mu}_{h}}\bigl[V_{h}^{\pi}(s_{h})-Q_{h}^{\pi}(s_{h},a_{h})\bigr]=J(\pi)-J(\mu). (43)

By Lemma 13 applied in the fake MDP (with reward r~\widetilde{r}, same dynamics) and using Eq. 42,

ℒμ​(π,f)=∑h=1H𝔼dhμ​[fh​(sh,π)−fh​(sh,ah)]=Jr~​(π)−Jr~​(μ)=f1​(s1,π)−𝔼μ​[R⁡(τ,r~)].\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi,f)=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{d^{\mu}_{h}}\bigl[f_{h}(s_{h},\pi)-f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})\bigr]=J_{\widetilde{r}}(\pi)-J_{\widetilde{r}}(\mu)=f_{1}(s_{1},\pi)-\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[R(\tau;\widetilde{r})]. (44)

Subtracting Eq. 44 from Eq. 43,

ℒμ(π,Qπ)−ℒμ(π,f)=[J⁡(π)−f1​(s1,π)]⏟=:A+[𝔼μ​[R⁡(τ,r~)]−J⁡(μ)]⏟=:B.\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi,Q^{\pi})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi,f)=\underbrace{\bigl[J(\pi)-f_{1}(s_{1},\pi)\bigr]}_{=:A}+\underbrace{\bigl[\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[R(\tau;\widetilde{r})]-J(\mu)\bigr]}_{=:B}. (45)

Step 2: express AA and BB as Bellman residuals of ff. By the definition of r~\widetilde{r} and 𝒯π​fh​(sh,ah)=r⋆​(sh,ah)+𝔼sh+1​[fh+1​(sh+1,π)]{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})=r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})+\mathbb{E}_{s_{h+1}}[f_{h+1}(s_{h+1},\pi)],

r⋆​(sh,ah)−r~h​(sh,ah)=𝒯π​fh​(sh,ah)−fh​(sh,ah).\displaystyle r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})-\widetilde{r}_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})={\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h}).

Taking expectations under dhπd^{\pi}_{h} and dhμd^{\mu}_{h} respectively and summing over hh,

A=𝔼τ∼π​[R⋆​(τ)−R⁡(τ,r~)]=∑h=1H𝔼dhπ​[(𝒯π​fh−fh)​(sh,ah)],\displaystyle A=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\pi}[R^{\star}(\tau)-R(\tau;\widetilde{r})]=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{d^{\pi}_{h}}\bigl[({\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}f_{h}-f_{h})(s_{h},a_{h})\bigr], (46)
B=𝔼τ∼μ​[R⁡(τ,r~)−R⋆​(τ)]=∑h=1H𝔼dhμ​[(fh−𝒯π​fh)​(sh,ah)].\displaystyle B=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\mu}[R(\tau;\widetilde{r})-R^{\star}(\tau)]=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{d^{\mu}_{h}}\bigl[(f_{h}-{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}f_{h})(s_{h},a_{h})\bigr]. (47)

Step 3: bound via Assumption 2. Combining Eq. 45–Eq. 47 and applying Jensen’s inequality (∥⋅∥1,ν≤∥⋅∥2,ν\|\cdot\|_{1,\nu}\leq\|\cdot\|_{2,\nu}) term-by-term,

|ℒμ​(π,Qπ)−ℒμ​(π,f)|≤∑h=1H‖fh−𝒯π​fh‖2,dhπ+∑h=1H‖fh−𝒯π​fh‖2,dhμ.\displaystyle\bigl|\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi,Q^{\pi})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi,f)\bigr|\leq\sum_{h=1}^{H}\bigl\|f_{h}-{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}f_{h}\bigr\|_{2,d^{\pi}_{h}}+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\bigl\|f_{h}-{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}f_{h}\bigr\|_{2,d^{\mu}_{h}}.

Since f=fπf=f_{\pi} attains the argmin\mathop{\mathrm{argmin}} in the definition of fπf_{\pi}, Assumption 2 gives

suph,ν‖fh−(𝒯π​f)h‖2,ν2≤εℱ.\sup_{h,\nu}\|f_{h}-({\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}f)_{h}\|_{2,\nu}^{2}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F}}.

Taking ν=dhπ\nu=d_{h}^{\pi} and ν=dhμ\nu=d_{h}^{\mu} gives ‖fh−𝒯π​fh‖2,ν2≤εℱ\|f_{h}-{\mathcal{T}}^{\pi}f_{h}\|_{2,\nu}^{2}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F}} for each h∈[H]h\in[H] and each ν∈{dhπ,dhμ}\nu\in\{d^{\pi}_{h},d^{\mu}_{h}\}. Summing 2​H2H such terms gives

|ℒμ​(π,Qπ)−ℒμ​(π,f)|≤2​H​εℱ,\displaystyle\bigl|\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi,Q^{\pi})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi,f)\bigr|\leq 2H\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F}}},

which is the claim. ∎

We recall the policy-loss notation used in the decomposition. For a distribution μ\mu,

ℒμ​(π,f)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi,f) ≔∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[fh​(sh,π⁡(sh))−fh​(sh,ah)].\displaystyle\coloneqq\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[f_{h}(s_{h},\pi(s_{h}))-f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})\big].
Lemma 15 (Regret Decomposition).

Let π\pi be an arbitrary competitor policy, π^∈Π\widehat{\pi}\in\Pi be some learned policy, r^∈ℛ\widehat{r}\in\mathcal{R} be some learned reward function, and f∈ℱf\in\mathcal{F} be an arbitrary function over 𝒮×𝒜{\mathcal{S}}\times\mathcal{A}. Then we have the following decomposition:

J⁡(π)−J⁡(π^)\displaystyle J(\pi)-J(\widehat{\pi}) =∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[𝒯r^π^​fh​(sh,ah)−fh​(sh,ah)]+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[fh​(sh,ah)−𝒯r^π^​fh​(sh,ah)]\displaystyle=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[{\mathcal{T}}_{{\widehat{r}}}^{\widehat{\pi}}f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-{\mathcal{T}}_{{\widehat{r}}}^{\widehat{\pi}}f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]
+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ[fh(sh,ah)−fh(sh,π^(sh))]−ℒμ(π^,Qπ^)+ℒμ(π^,f)\displaystyle+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-f_{h}(s_{h},\widehat{\pi}(s_{h}))\big]-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},Q^{\widehat{\pi}})+\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},f)
+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ[r⋆(sh,ah)−r^(sh,ah)]+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ[r^(sh,ah)−r⋆(sh,ah)].\displaystyle+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})-{\widehat{r}}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[{\widehat{r}}(s_{h},a_{h})-r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})\big].
Proof.

Define rhf,π^​(sh,ah)≔fh​(sh,ah)−𝔼sh+1​[fh+1​(sh+1,π^)]r_{h}^{f,\widehat{\pi}}(s_{h},a_{h})\coloneqq f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-\mathbb{E}_{s_{h+1}}[f_{h+1}(s_{h+1},\widehat{\pi})]. Then rf,π^=(r1f,π^,…,rHf,π^)r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}=(r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}_{1},\ldots,r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}_{H}) is a fake reward function given ff and π^\widehat{\pi}, with trajectory return R⁡(τ,rf,π^)R(\tau;r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}). We use the subscript (⋅)rf,π^(\cdot)_{r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}} to denote functions or operators under another MDP ℳrf,π^\mathcal{M}_{r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}, which have the same dynamics with ℳ\mathcal{M}. The only difference is ℳrf,π^\mathcal{M}_{r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}} has a reward function rf,π^r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}. As the policy π(⋅∣s)\pi(\cdot\mid s) and the transition kernel P(⋅∣s,a)P(\cdot\mid s,a) has no relationship with rewards, we get the same distribution dπd^{\pi}, no matter under MDP ℳ\mathcal{M} or ℳrf,π^\mathcal{M}_{r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}.

Since ff satisfies the Bellman equation with respect to ℳrf,π^\mathcal{M}_{r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}, i.e. fh​(sh,ah)=rhf,π^​(sh,ah)+𝔼sh+1​[fh+1​(sh+1,π^)]f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})=r_{h}^{f,\widehat{\pi}}(s_{h},a_{h})+\mathbb{E}_{s_{h+1}}[f_{h+1}(s_{h+1},\widehat{\pi})], we know fh=Qhπ^,rf,π^f_{h}=Q_{h}^{\widehat{\pi},r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}, for h∈[H]h\in[H].

We perform a performance decomposition:

J⁡(π)−J⁡(π^)=J⁡(π)−J⁡(μ)−(J⁡(π^)−J⁡(μ)).\displaystyle J(\pi)-J(\widehat{\pi})=J(\pi)-J(\mu)-(J(\widehat{\pi})-J(\mu)). (48)

By performance difference lemma 13,

J⁡(π^)−J⁡(μ)\displaystyle J(\widehat{\pi})-J(\mu) =−(J⁡(μ)−J⁡(π^))\displaystyle=-\big(J(\mu)-J(\widehat{\pi})\big)
=−(∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[Qhπ^​(sh,ah)−Vhπ^​(sh)])\displaystyle=-\bigg(\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[Q_{h}^{\widehat{\pi}}(s_{h},a_{h})-V_{h}^{\widehat{\pi}}(s_{h})\big]\bigg)
=∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[Vhπ^​(sh)−Qhπ^​(sh,ah)]\displaystyle=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[V_{h}^{\widehat{\pi}}(s_{h})-Q_{h}^{\widehat{\pi}}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]
=ℒμ​(π^,Qπ^).\displaystyle=\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},Q^{\widehat{\pi}}).

Define Δ⁡(π^)≔ℒμ​(π^,Qπ^)−ℒμ​(π^,f)\Delta(\widehat{\pi})\coloneqq\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},Q^{\widehat{\pi}})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},f), then we can rewrite the second term of Eq. 48 as

J⁡(π^)−J⁡(μ)\displaystyle J(\widehat{\pi})-J(\mu) =ℒμ​(π^,Qπ^)\displaystyle=\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},Q^{\widehat{\pi}})
=Δ⁡(π^)+ℒμ​(π^,f)\displaystyle=\Delta(\widehat{\pi})+\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},f)
=Δ⁡(π^)+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[fh​(sh,π^​(sh))−fh​(sh,ah)]\displaystyle=\Delta(\widehat{\pi})+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[f_{h}(s_{h},\widehat{\pi}(s_{h}))-f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]
=Δ⁡(π^)+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[Vhπ^,rf,π^​(sh)−Qhπ^,rf,π^​(sh,ah)]\displaystyle=\Delta(\widehat{\pi})+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[V_{h}^{\widehat{\pi},r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}(s_{h})-Q_{h}^{\widehat{\pi},r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]
=Δ⁡(π^)+Jrf,π^​(π^)−Jrf,π^​(μ)\displaystyle=\Delta(\widehat{\pi})+J_{r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}(\widehat{\pi})-J_{r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}(\mu) (Performance difference lemma 13)
=Δ⁡(π^)+V1π^,rf,π^​(s1)−𝔼τ∼μ​[R⁡(τ,rf,π^)]\displaystyle=\Delta(\widehat{\pi})+V_{1}^{\widehat{\pi},r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}(s_{1})-\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\mu}[R(\tau;r^{f,\widehat{\pi}})]
=Δ⁡(π^)+f1​(s1,π^)−𝔼τ∼μ​[R⁡(τ,rf,π^)].\displaystyle=\Delta(\widehat{\pi})+f_{1}(s_{1},\widehat{\pi})-\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\mu}[R(\tau;r^{f,\widehat{\pi}})].

Substituting this identity into Eq. 48 gives

J⁡(π)−J⁡(π^)=(J⁡(π)−f1​(s1,π^))+(𝔼τ∼μ​[R⁡(τ,rf,π^)]−J⁡(μ))−Δ⁡(π^).\displaystyle J(\pi)-J(\widehat{\pi})=\bigl(J(\pi)-f_{1}(s_{1},\widehat{\pi})\bigr)+\bigl(\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\mu}[R(\tau;r^{f,\widehat{\pi}})]-J(\mu)\bigr)-\Delta(\widehat{\pi}). (49)

By the definition of the expected return J⁡(μ)J(\mu),

𝔼τ∼μ​[R⁡(τ,rf,π^)]−J⁡(μ)\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\mu}[R(\tau;r^{f,\widehat{\pi}})]-J(\mu) =𝔼τ∼μ​[R⁡(τ,rf,π^)−R⋆​(τ)]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\mu}\big[R(\tau;r^{f,\widehat{\pi}})-R^{\star}(\tau)\big]
=∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[rf,π^​(sh,ah)−r⋆​(sh,ah)]\displaystyle=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}(s_{h},a_{h})-r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]
=∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[fh​(sh,ah)−𝔼sh+1​[fh+1​(sh+1,π^)]−r⋆​(sh,ah)]\displaystyle=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}[f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-\mathbb{E}_{s_{h+1}}[f_{h+1}(s_{h+1},\widehat{\pi})]-r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})] (Definition of rf,π^r^{f,\widehat{\pi}})
=∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[fh​(sh,ah)−𝒯π^​(sh,ah)].\displaystyle=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-{\mathcal{T}}^{\widehat{\pi}}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]. (50)

Since J⁡(π)=∑h=1H𝔼dhπ​[r⋆​(sh,ah)]=𝔼τ∼π​[R⋆​(τ)]J(\pi)=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{d^{\pi}_{h}}[r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})]=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\pi}[R^{\star}(\tau)],

J⁡(π)−f1​(s1,π^)\displaystyle J(\pi)-f_{1}(s_{1},\widehat{\pi}) =(J⁡(π)−𝔼τ∼π​[R⁡(τ,rf,π^)])+(𝔼τ∼π​[R⁡(τ,rf,π^)]−f1​(s1,π^))\displaystyle=(J(\pi)-\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\pi}[R(\tau;r^{f,\widehat{\pi}})])+(\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\pi}[R(\tau;r^{f,\widehat{\pi}})]-f_{1}(s_{1},\widehat{\pi}))
=∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[r⋆​(sh,ah)−rf,π^​(sh,ah)]+Jrf,π^​(π)−Jrf,π^​(π^)\displaystyle=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}[r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})-r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}(s_{h},a_{h})]+J_{r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}(\pi)-J_{r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}(\widehat{\pi})
=∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[𝒯π^​f​(sh,ah)−f⁡(sh,ah)]+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[Qhπ^,rf,π^​(sh,ah)−Vhπ^,rf,π^​(sh)]\displaystyle=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[{\mathcal{T}}^{\widehat{\pi}}f(s_{h},a_{h})-f(s_{h},a_{h})\big]+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[Q_{h}^{\widehat{\pi},r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}(s_{h},a_{h})-V_{h}^{\widehat{\pi},r^{f,\widehat{\pi}}}(s_{h})\big]
=∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[𝒯π^​f​(sh,ah)−f⁡(sh,ah)]+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[fh​(sh,ah)−fh​(sh,π^​(sh))].\displaystyle=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[{\mathcal{T}}^{\widehat{\pi}}f(s_{h},a_{h})-f(s_{h},a_{h})\big]+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-f_{h}(s_{h},\widehat{\pi}(s_{h}))\big]. (51)

Putting Eq. 50,Eq. 51 into Eq. 49, we get

J⁡(π)−J⁡(π^)\displaystyle J(\pi)-J(\widehat{\pi}) =∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[𝒯π^​fh​(sh,ah)−fh​(sh,ah)]+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[fh​(sh,ah)−fh​(sh,π^​(sh))]\displaystyle=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[{\mathcal{T}}^{\widehat{\pi}}f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-f_{h}(s_{h},\widehat{\pi}(s_{h}))\big]
+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ[fh(sh,ah)−𝒯π^fh(sh,ah)]−ℒμ(π^,Qπ^)+ℒμ(π^,f).\displaystyle+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-{\mathcal{T}}^{\widehat{\pi}}f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},Q^{\widehat{\pi}})+\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},f). (52)

For a given learned reward function r^{\widehat{r}}, we can write

𝒯π^​fh​(sh,ah)\displaystyle{\mathcal{T}}^{{\widehat{\pi}}}f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h}) =r⋆(sh,ah)+𝔼sh+1∼P(⋅∣sh,ah)[fh+1(sh+1,π^(sh+1))]\displaystyle=r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})+\mathbb{E}_{s_{h+1}\sim P(\cdot\mid s_{h},a_{h})}\big[f_{h+1}(s_{h+1},{\widehat{\pi}}(s_{h+1}))\big]

+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ[fh(sh,ah)−fh(sh,π^(sh))]−ℒμ(π^,Qπ^)+ℒμ(π^,f)\displaystyle+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[f_{h}(s_{h},a_{h})-f_{h}(s_{h},\widehat{\pi}(s_{h}))\big]-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},Q^{\widehat{\pi}})+\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\widehat{\pi},f)
+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ[r⋆(sh,ah)−r^(sh,ah)]+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ[r^(sh,ah)−r⋆(sh,ah)].\displaystyle+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})-{\widehat{r}}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[{\widehat{r}}(s_{h},a_{h})-r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})\big].

∎

Appendix C Proof of the Outcome-Based Offline RL Upper Bound

In this section we prove Theorem 1, using the population losses defined in Eq. 18.

C.1 Regret Decomposition

Our objective is to find an upper bound for

J⁡(π)−J⁡(π¯)=1K​∑k=1K(J⁡(π)−J⁡(πk)).\displaystyle J(\pi)-J(\bar{\pi})=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\big(J(\pi)-J(\pi_{k})\big).

+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[fk,h​(sh,ah)−fk,h​(sh,πk​(sh))]⏟(II)k+ℒμ​(πk,fk)−ℒμ​(πk,Qπk)⏟(III)k\displaystyle+\underbrace{\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[f_{k,h}(s_{h},a_{h})-f_{k,h}(s_{h},\pi_{k}(s_{h}))\big]}_{(\mathrm{II})_{k}}+\underbrace{\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},f_{k})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},Q^{\pi_{k}})}_{(\mathrm{III})_{k}}
+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[r⋆​(sh,ah)−rk​(sh,ah)]+∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[rk​(sh,ah)−r⋆​(sh,ah)]⏟(IV)k.\displaystyle+\underbrace{\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})-r_{k}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]+\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[r_{k}(s_{h},a_{h})-r^{\star}(s_{h},a_{h})\big]}_{(\mathrm{IV})_{k}}. (53)

C.2 Bounding the Policy-Optimization Term

Term (II)k=∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhπ​[fk,h​(sh,ah)−fk,h​(sh,πk​(sh))](\mathrm{II})_{k}=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\pi}_{h}}\big[f_{k,h}(s_{h},a_{h})-f_{k,h}(s_{h},\pi_{k}(s_{h}))\big] is controlled by the no-regret property of the layer-wise softmax update Eq. 5. because dhπ​(s,a)=dh,Sπ​(s)​πh​(a∣s)d_{h}^{\pi}(s,a)=d_{h,S}^{\pi}(s)\pi_{h}(a\mid s). Choosing η=η⋆=Vmax​K/(8​log⁡|𝒜|)\eta=\eta^{\star}=V_{\max}\sqrt{K/(8\log|\mathcal{A}|)}, Eq. 20 yields

1K​∑k=1K(II)k≤H​Vmax​log⁡|𝒜|2​K=O~​(H​VmaxK).\displaystyle\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}(\mathrm{II})_{k}\leq HV_{\max}\sqrt{\frac{\log|\mathcal{A}|}{2K}}=\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{HV_{\max}}{\sqrt{K}}\right). (54)

C.3 Bounding the Bellman and Reward-Mismatch Terms

Recall the state–action concentrability Cs​a​(π)C_{sa}(\pi) from Eq. 2. For any g:𝒮h×𝒜→ℝg:{\mathcal{S}}_{h}\times\mathcal{A}\to\mathbb{R}, the pointwise bound dhπ​(s,a)≤Cs​a​(π)​dhμ​(s,a)d_{h}^{\pi}(s,a)\leq C_{sa}(\pi)d_{h}^{\mu}(s,a) gives

𝔼dhπ​[g​(sh,ah)2]≤Cs​a​(π)​𝔼dhμ​[g​(sh,ah)2].\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{d^{\pi}_{h}}[g(s_{h},a_{h})^{2}]\leq C_{sa}(\pi)\mathbb{E}_{d^{\mu}_{h}}[g(s_{h},a_{h})^{2}].

(I)k≤H​(Cs​a​(π)+1)β+β2​∑h=1H𝔼sh,ah∼dhμ​[((𝒯rkπk​fk−fk)​(sh,ah))2].\displaystyle(\mathrm{I})_{k}\leq\frac{H(C_{sa}(\pi)+1)}{\beta}+\frac{\beta}{2}\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{s_{h},a_{h}\sim d^{\mu}_{h}}\big[(({\mathcal{T}}_{r_{k}}^{\pi_{k}}f_{k}-f_{k})(s_{h},a_{h}))^{2}\big]. (55)

where in the last inequality we used H​Cs​a​(π)+1≤H⁡(Cs​a​(π)+1)HC_{sa}(\pi)+1\leq H(C_{sa}(\pi)+1) and the definitions Eq. 18.

C.4 Pessimism and Empirical Transfer

Now fix the high-probability event on which the concentration and approximation lemmas from Sections B.2 and B.3 hold simultaneously for every π∈Π\pi\in\Pi, r∈ℛr\in\mathcal{R}, and f∈ℱf\in\mathcal{F}. Because the change-of-measure step Eq. 57 produces the coefficient β/2\beta/2 on the population BE/RM losses, and the Bellman-error (Lemma 11) and reward-model (Lemma 10) concentration inequalities introduce a factor 22 in front of the empirical losses, the two factors cancel so that the pessimistic evaluation step Eq. 4 is invoked with the algorithmic coefficient β\beta. On this event we have, for every k∈[K]k\in[K],

ℒμBE​(πk,rk,fk)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{BE}}(\pi_{k},r_{k},f_{k}) ≤2​ℒ𝒟BE​(πk,rk,fk)+εBE+4​εℱ,ℱ,\displaystyle\leq 2\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathrm{BE}}(\pi_{k},r_{k},f_{k})+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{BE}}+4\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F},\mathcal{F}}, (58a)
ℒμRM​(rk)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{RM}}(r_{k}) ≤2​[ℒ𝒟RM​(rk)−ℒ𝒟RM​(r⋆)]+εRM,\displaystyle\leq 2\bigl[\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathrm{RM}}(r_{k})-\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathrm{RM}}(r^{\star})\bigr]+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{RM}}, (58b)
supπ∈Π,f∈ℱ|ℒμ​(π,f)−ℒ𝒟​(π,f)|\displaystyle\sup_{\pi\in\Pi,f\in\mathcal{F}}\bigl|\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi,f)-\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi,f)\bigr| ≤εPerf,\displaystyle\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Perf}}}, (58c)
|ℒμ​(πk,Qπk)−ℒμ​(πk,fπk)|\displaystyle|\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},Q^{\pi_{k}})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},f_{\pi_{k}})| ≤O(Hεℱ)(Lemma 14).\displaystyle\leq O(H\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F}}})\quad\text{(\lx@cref{creftypecap~refnum}{lemma:bound-diff-Q-and-f_pi})}. (58d)

We now bound the quantity

Δk≔β2​ℒμBE​(πk,rk,fk)+β2​ℒμRM​(rk)+ℒμ​(πk,fk)−ℒμ​(πk,Qπk)\displaystyle\Delta_{k}\coloneqq\frac{\beta}{2}\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{BE}}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},r_{k},f_{k})+\frac{\beta}{2}\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{RM}}(r_{k})+\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},f_{k})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},Q^{\pi_{k}})

that appears on the right-hand side of Eq. 57, in four explicit steps.

Step (A): transfer BE/RM losses to the empirical data. Using Eq. 58a–Eq. 58b,

β2​ℒμBE​(πk,rk,fk)+β2​ℒμRM​(rk)≤β​ℒ𝒟BE​(πk,rk,fk)+β⁡[ℒ𝒟RM​(rk)−ℒ𝒟RM​(r⋆)]+β2​(εBE+εRM+4​εℱ,ℱ).\displaystyle\frac{\beta}{2}\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{BE}}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},r_{k},f_{k})+\frac{\beta}{2}\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{RM}}(r_{k})\leq\beta\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{BE}}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},r_{k},f_{k})+\beta\bigl[\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathrm{RM}}(r_{k})-\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathrm{RM}}(r^{\star})\bigr]+\frac{\beta}{2}\bigl(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{BE}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{RM}}+4\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F},\mathcal{F}}\bigr). (59)

The r⋆r^{\star}-centred form is essential under noisy observations, but it cancels exactly when the same quantity is subtracted from the pessimism RHS in Step (D) below.

Step (B): transfer the performance-loss gap ℒμ​(πk,fk)−ℒμ​(πk,Qπk)\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},f_{k})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},Q^{\pi_{k}}) to the empirical data. Insert fπkf_{\pi_{k}} as a pivot and use Eq. 58c together with Eq. 58d:

ℒμ​(πk,fk)−ℒμ​(πk,Qπk)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},f_{k})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},Q^{\pi_{k}}) =[ℒμ​(πk,fk)−ℒ𝒟​(πk,fk)]⏟≤εPerf​ by Eq. 58c\displaystyle=\underbrace{\bigl[\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},f_{k})-\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f_{k})\bigr]}_{\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Perf}}}\text{ by }\lx@cref{creftype~refnum}{eq:conc-Perf}}
+[ℒ𝒟​(πk,fπk)−ℒμ​(πk,fπk)]⏟≤εPerf​ by Eq. 58c\displaystyle\quad+\underbrace{\bigl[\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f_{\pi_{k}})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},f_{\pi_{k}})\bigr]}_{\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Perf}}}\text{ by }\lx@cref{creftype~refnum}{eq:conc-Perf}}
+[ℒμ​(πk,fπk)−ℒμ​(πk,Qπk)]⏟≤O⁡(H​εℱ)​ by Eq. 58d\displaystyle\quad+\underbrace{\bigl[\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},f_{\pi_{k}})-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}(\pi_{k},Q^{\pi_{k}})\bigr]}_{\leq O(H\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F}}})\text{ by }\lx@cref{creftype~refnum}{eq:conc-apx}}
+ℒ𝒟​(πk,fk)−ℒ𝒟​(πk,fπk)\displaystyle\quad+\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f_{k})-\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f_{\pi_{k}})
≤ℒ𝒟​(πk,fk)−ℒ𝒟​(πk,fπk)+2​εPerf+O⁡(H​εℱ),\displaystyle\leq\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f_{k})-\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f_{\pi_{k}})+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Perf}}}+O(H\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathcal{F}}}), (60)

where we applied the uniform concentration Eq. 58c twice (once to (πk,fk)∈Π×ℱ(\pi_{k},f_{k})\in\Pi\times\mathcal{F} and once to (πk,fπk)∈Π×ℱ(\pi_{k},f_{\pi_{k}})\in\Pi\times\mathcal{F}; the latter uses fπk∈ℱf_{\pi_{k}}\in\mathcal{F} from Lemma 12).

Step (C): invoke pessimistic optimality at coefficient β\beta. By the definition of the pessimistic estimator Eq. 4, (fk,rk)∈ℱ×ℛ(f_{k},r_{k})\in\mathcal{F}\times\mathcal{R} minimises

(f,r)↦ℒ𝒟​(πk,f)+β​ℒ𝒟BE​(πk,r,f)+β​ℒ𝒟RM​(r).\displaystyle(f,r)\mapsto\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f)+\beta\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{BE}}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},r,f)+\beta\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{RM}}_{\mathcal{D}}(r). (4)

Plugging in the comparator (fπk,r⋆)∈ℱ×ℛ(f_{\pi_{k}},r^{\star})\in\mathcal{F}\times\mathcal{R} (using fπk∈ℱf_{\pi_{k}}\in\mathcal{F} from Assumption 2 and r⋆∈ℛr^{\star}\in\mathcal{R} from Assumption 1) yields

ℒ𝒟​(πk,fk)+β​ℒ𝒟BE​(πk,rk,fk)+β​ℒ𝒟RM​(rk)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f_{k})+\beta\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{BE}}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},r_{k},f_{k})+\beta\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{RM}}_{\mathcal{D}}(r_{k})
≤ℒ𝒟​(πk,fπk)+β​ℒ𝒟BE​(πk,r⋆,fπk)+β​ℒ𝒟RM​(r⋆).\displaystyle\qquad\leq\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f_{\pi_{k}})+\beta\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{BE}}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},r^{\star},f_{\pi_{k}})+\beta\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{RM}}_{\mathcal{D}}(r^{\star}). (61)

Step (D): bound the comparator Bellman-error loss, and cancel ℒ𝒟RM​(r⋆)\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathrm{RM}}(r^{\star}). Subtracting β​ℒ𝒟RM​(r⋆)\beta\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathrm{RM}}(r^{\star}) from both sides of Eq. 61 gives the r⋆r^{\star}-centred pessimism inequality

ℒ𝒟​(πk,fk)+β​ℒ𝒟BE​(πk,rk,fk)+β⁡[ℒ𝒟RM​(rk)−ℒ𝒟RM​(r⋆)]\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f_{k})+\beta\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{BE}}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},r_{k},f_{k})+\beta\bigl[\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{RM}}_{\mathcal{D}}(r_{k})-\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{RM}}_{\mathcal{D}}(r^{\star})\bigr]
≤ℒ𝒟​(πk,fπk)+β​ℒ𝒟BE​(πk,r⋆,fπk).\displaystyle\qquad\leq\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},f_{\pi_{k}})+\beta\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{BE}}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},r^{\star},f_{\pi_{k}}). (62)

By Lemma 12, the remaining comparator Bellman-error term on the RHS is controlled by

β​ℒ𝒟BE​(πk,r⋆,fπk)≤β​εapx.\displaystyle\beta\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{BE}}_{\mathcal{D}}(\pi_{k},r^{\star},f_{\pi_{k}})\leq\beta\varepsilon_{\mathrm{apx}}. (63)

Combining (A)–(D). Adding Eq. 59 and Eq. 60 gives

Appendix D Proof of the Preference-Based Upper Bound

We prove Theorem 3. In this cumulative-return setting, Vmax=HV_{\max}=H and every candidate trajectory return lies in [0,H][0,H]. The argument follows the proof of Theorem 1. The policy and Bellman empirical losses use the 2​n2n unlabelled trajectories contained in the preference pairs; since these trajectories are i.i.d. from μ\mu, the corresponding concentration bounds change only by universal constants. Relative to the scalar-outcome proof, the main changes are that the squared reward-model loss is replaced by the logistic preference loss, and the reward-mismatch term is controlled through a centered change-of-measure step, since preferences identify rewards only up to uniform shifts of cumulative returns.

We use the following constants for the fixed BTL model on the return range [0,H][0,H]:

αC\displaystyle\alpha_{\mathrm{C}} ≔γ22​inf|w|≤Hexp⁡(γ​w)(1+exp⁡(γ​w))2,\displaystyle\coloneqq\frac{\gamma^{2}}{2}\inf_{|w|\leq H}\frac{\exp(\gamma w)}{(1+\exp(\gamma w))^{2}},
aC\displaystyle a_{\mathrm{C}} ≔11+eγ​H,BC≔log⁡1−aCaC,\displaystyle\coloneqq\frac{1}{1+e^{\gamma H}},\qquad B_{\mathrm{C}}\coloneqq\log\frac{1-a_{\mathrm{C}}}{a_{\mathrm{C}}},
bC\displaystyle b_{\mathrm{C}} ≔supp,q∈[aC,1−aC],p≠qp​log2⁡(p/q)+(1−p)​log2⁡((1−p)/(1−q))KL(Bern(p)∥Bern(q)),cC≔2​bC+83​BC.\displaystyle\coloneqq\sup_{p,q\in[a_{\mathrm{C}},1-a_{\mathrm{C}}],p\neq q}\frac{p\log^{2}(p/q)+(1-p)\log^{2}((1-p)/(1-q))}{\mathrm{KL}(\mathrm{Bern}(p)\|\mathrm{Bern}(q))},\qquad c_{\mathrm{C}}\coloneqq 2b_{\mathrm{C}}+\frac{8}{3}B_{\mathrm{C}}. (66)

These constants depend only on γ\gamma and HH.

D.1 Preference Identifiability and Concentration

For a pair (τ+,τ−)(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}), define the return-difference notation

Δr​(τ+,τ−)≔R⁡(τ+,r)−R⁡(τ−,r),Δ⋆​(τ+,τ−)≔Δr⋆​(τ+,τ−).\Delta_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-})\coloneqq R(\tau^{+};r)-R(\tau^{-};r),\qquad\Delta^{\star}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-})\coloneqq\Delta_{r^{\star}}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}).

Let

ℓr​(τ+,τ−,y)≔−y​log⁡Cr​(τ+,τ−)−(1−y)​log⁡(1−Cr​(τ+,τ−))\ell_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-},y)\coloneqq-y\log\mathrm{C}_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-})-(1-y)\log(1-\mathrm{C}_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}))

be the BTL log loss induced by rr. The population preference loss is

ℒμPref​(r)≔𝔼τ+,τ−∼μ,y|τ±​[ℓr​(τ+,τ−,y)].\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r)\coloneqq\mathbb{E}_{\tau^{+},\tau^{-}\sim\mu,y\mid\tau^{\pm}}\bigl[\ell_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-},y)\bigr].
Lemma 16 (BTL preference identifiability).

Under the BTL model Eq. 8, with αC\alpha_{\mathrm{C}} defined in Eq. 66, for every r∈ℛr\in\mathcal{R},

ℒμPref​(r)−ℒμPref​(r⋆)≥αC​𝔼μ⊗μ​[(Δr−Δ⋆)2]=2​αC​Varμ​(R⁡(⋅,r)−R⋆​(⋅)).\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r)-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r^{\star})\geq\alpha_{\mathrm{C}}\mathbb{E}_{\mu\otimes\mu}\left[(\Delta_{r}-\Delta^{\star})^{2}\right]=2\alpha_{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Var}_{\mu}\left(R(\cdot;r)-R^{\star}(\cdot)\right).

Equivalently,

Varμ​(R⁡(⋅,r)−R⋆​(⋅))≤12​αC​(ℒμPref​(r)−ℒμPref​(r⋆)).\mathrm{Var}_{\mu}\left(R(\cdot;r)-R^{\star}(\cdot)\right)\leq\frac{1}{2\alpha_{\mathrm{C}}}\bigl(\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r)-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r^{\star})\bigr).
Proof.

Fix a trajectory pair (τ+,τ−)(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}). Write

dr=Δr​(τ+,τ−),d⋆=Δ⋆​(τ+,τ−).d_{r}=\Delta_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}),\qquad d_{\star}=\Delta^{\star}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}).

Since R⁡(τ,r)∈[0,H]R(\tau;r)\in[0,H], both drd_{r} and d⋆d_{\star} lie in [−H,H][-H,H]. Define the one-dimensional logistic link

sγ​(w)=exp⁡(γ​w)1+exp⁡(γ​w).s_{\gamma}(w)=\frac{\exp(\gamma w)}{1+\exp(\gamma w)}.

For this fixed pair, the true label distribution is

y∼Bern⁡(sγ​(d⋆)).y\sim\mathrm{Bern}(s_{\gamma}(d_{\star})).

Let p⋆=sγ​(d⋆)p_{\star}=s_{\gamma}(d_{\star}) and define the conditional log-risk

ϕ⁡(w)=−p⋆​log⁡sγ​(w)−(1−p⋆)​log⁡(1−sγ​(w)).\phi(w)=-p_{\star}\log s_{\gamma}(w)-(1-p_{\star})\log(1-s_{\gamma}(w)).

Then

𝔼y​[ℓr​(τ+,τ−,y)]=ϕ⁡(dr),𝔼y​[ℓr⋆​(τ+,τ−,y)]=ϕ⁡(d⋆).\mathbb{E}_{y}[\ell_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-},y)]=\phi(d_{r}),\qquad\mathbb{E}_{y}[\ell_{r^{\star}}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-},y)]=\phi(d_{\star}).

A direct differentiation gives

ϕ′​(w)=γ⁡(sγ​(w)−p⋆),ϕ′′​(w)=γ2​sγ​(w)​(1−sγ​(w)).\phi^{\prime}(w)=\gamma\bigl(s_{\gamma}(w)-p_{\star}\bigr),\qquad\phi^{\prime\prime}(w)=\gamma^{2}s_{\gamma}(w)(1-s_{\gamma}(w)).

Since p⋆=sγ​(d⋆)p_{\star}=s_{\gamma}(d_{\star}), we have ϕ′​(d⋆)=0\phi^{\prime}(d_{\star})=0. Also,

mC≔inf|w|≤Hγ2​sγ​(w)​(1−sγ​(w))>0,m_{\mathrm{C}}\coloneqq\inf_{|w|\leq H}\gamma^{2}s_{\gamma}(w)(1-s_{\gamma}(w))>0,

because sγ​(w)​(1−sγ​(w))s_{\gamma}(w)(1-s_{\gamma}(w)) is continuous and strictly positive on the compact interval [−H,H][-H,H]. Taylor’s theorem with remainder gives, for some point w¯\bar{w} between drd_{r} and d⋆d_{\star},

ϕ⁡(dr)−ϕ⁡(d⋆)=ϕ′​(d⋆)​(dr−d⋆)+12​ϕ′′​(w¯)​(dr−d⋆)2≥mC2​(dr−d⋆)2.\phi(d_{r})-\phi(d_{\star})=\phi^{\prime}(d_{\star})(d_{r}-d_{\star})+\frac{1}{2}\phi^{\prime\prime}(\bar{w})(d_{r}-d_{\star})^{2}\geq\frac{m_{\mathrm{C}}}{2}(d_{r}-d_{\star})^{2}.

By the definition of αC\alpha_{\mathrm{C}} in Eq. 66, mC/2=αCm_{\mathrm{C}}/2=\alpha_{\mathrm{C}}. Since the trajectory pair was arbitrary, taking expectation over τ+,τ−∼μ\tau^{+},\tau^{-}\sim\mu gives

ℒμPref​(r)−ℒμPref​(r⋆)≥αC​𝔼μ⊗μ​[(Δr−Δ⋆)2].\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r)-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r^{\star})\geq\alpha_{\mathrm{C}}\mathbb{E}_{\mu\otimes\mu}\left[(\Delta_{r}-\Delta^{\star})^{2}\right].

It remains to rewrite the pairwise error as a variance. Let

g⁡(τ)=R⁡(τ,r)−R⋆​(τ).g(\tau)=R(\tau;r)-R^{\star}(\tau).

Δr​(τ+,τ−)−Δ⋆​(τ+,τ−)=g⁡(τ+)−g⁡(τ−).\Delta_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-})-\Delta^{\star}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-})=g(\tau^{+})-g(\tau^{-}).

𝔼μ⊗μ​[(g⁡(τ+)−g⁡(τ−))2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\mu\otimes\mu}[(g(\tau^{+})-g(\tau^{-}))^{2}] =𝔼μ​[g​(τ)2]+𝔼μ​[g​(τ)2]−2​𝔼μ​[g⁡(τ)]2\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[g(\tau)^{2}]+\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[g(\tau)^{2}]-2\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[g(\tau)]^{2}
=2​Varμ​(g),\displaystyle=2\mathrm{Var}_{\mu}(g),

as desired. ∎

Lemma 17 (Preference log loss concentration).

Let aCa_{\mathrm{C}}, BCB_{\mathrm{C}}, bCb_{\mathrm{C}}, and cCc_{\mathrm{C}} be defined in Eq. 66. With probability at least 1−δ1-\delta, simultaneously for all r∈ℛr\in\mathcal{R},

ℒμPref​(r)−ℒμPref​(r⋆)≤2​[ℒ𝒟PrefPref​(r)−ℒ𝒟PrefPref​(r⋆)]+cC​log⁡(|ℛ|/δ)n.\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r)-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r^{\star})\leq 2\Bigl[\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{Pref}}}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r)-\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{Pref}}}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r^{\star})\Bigr]+c_{\mathrm{C}}\frac{\log(|\mathcal{R}|/\delta)}{n}.
Proof.

The structure is the same as the r⋆r^{\star}-centred reward-model concentration in Lemma 10: we control the population excess loss by the empirical loss difference relative to r⋆r^{\star}. The difference is that the random variable is now a log-likelihood ratio, whose mean is a KL divergence and whose variance is self-bounded by that same KL divergence.

Fix r∈ℛr\in\mathcal{R}. Let Z=(τ+,τ−,y)Z=(\tau^{+},\tau^{-},y) and let P⋆P_{\star} denote the true law of ZZ: the pair (τ+,τ−)(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}) is drawn from μ⊗μ\mu\otimes\mu, and then

y|τ+,τ−∼Bern⁡(Cr⋆​(τ+,τ−)).y\mid\tau^{+},\tau^{-}\sim\mathrm{Bern}\bigl(\mathrm{C}_{r^{\star}}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-})\bigr).

Let PrP_{r} be the same law except that the conditional Bernoulli success probability is Cr​(τ+,τ−)\mathrm{C}_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}). Since the pair marginal is the same under P⋆P_{\star} and PrP_{r}, only the conditional Bernoulli law changes.

Write p⋆=Cr⋆​(τ+,τ−)p_{\star}=\mathrm{C}_{r^{\star}}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}) and pr=Cr​(τ+,τ−)p_{r}=\mathrm{C}_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}). Since P⋆P_{\star} and PrP_{r} have the same pair distribution, their likelihood ratio is just the Bernoulli label likelihood ratio. Thus

ℓr​(τ+,τ−,y)−ℓr⋆​(τ+,τ−,y)\displaystyle\ell_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-},y)-\ell_{r^{\star}}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-},y) =[−y​log⁡pr−(1−y)​log⁡(1−pr)]\displaystyle=\left[-y\log p_{r}-(1-y)\log(1-p_{r})\right]
−[−y​log⁡p⋆−(1−y)​log⁡(1−p⋆)]\displaystyle-\left[-y\log p_{\star}-(1-y)\log(1-p_{\star})\right]
=y​log⁡p⋆pr+(1−y)​log⁡1−p⋆1−pr\displaystyle=y\log\frac{p_{\star}}{p_{r}}+(1-y)\log\frac{1-p_{\star}}{1-p_{r}}
=log⁡p⋆y​(1−p⋆)1−ypry​(1−pr)1−y.\displaystyle=\log\frac{p_{\star}^{y}(1-p_{\star})^{1-y}}{p_{r}^{y}(1-p_{r})^{1-y}}.

Thus the single-sample loss difference is exactly the log-likelihood ratio:

Wr​(Z)≔ℓr​(τ+,τ−,y)−ℓr⋆​(τ+,τ−,y)=log⁡P⋆​(y∣τ+,τ−)Pr​(y∣τ+,τ−).W_{r}(Z)\coloneqq\ell_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-},y)-\ell_{r^{\star}}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-},y)=\log\frac{P_{\star}(y\mid\tau^{+},\tau^{-})}{P_{r}(y\mid\tau^{+},\tau^{-})}.

For this fixed trajectory pair, taking expectation only over the label y|τ+,τ−y\mid\tau^{+},\tau^{-} gives

𝔼y|τ+,τ−​[Wr​(Z)]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{y\mid\tau^{+},\tau^{-}}[W_{r}(Z)] =p⋆​log⁡p⋆pr+(1−p⋆)​log⁡1−p⋆1−pr\displaystyle=p_{\star}\log\frac{p_{\star}}{p_{r}}+(1-p_{\star})\log\frac{1-p_{\star}}{1-p_{r}}
=KL(Bern(p⋆)∥Bern(pr)).\displaystyle=\mathrm{KL}\left(\mathrm{Bern}(p_{\star})\|\mathrm{Bern}(p_{r})\right).

Now taking the outer expectation over the trajectory pair (τ+,τ−)∼μ⊗μ(\tau^{+},\tau^{-})\sim\mu\otimes\mu,

ℒμPref​(r)−ℒμPref​(r⋆)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r)-\mathcal{L}_{\mu}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r^{\star}) =𝔼(τ+,τ−)∼μ⊗μ​[𝔼y|τ+,τ−​[Wr​(Z)]]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{(\tau^{+},\tau^{-})\sim\mu\otimes\mu}\left[\mathbb{E}_{y\mid\tau^{+},\tau^{-}}[W_{r}(Z)]\right]
=𝔼Z∼P⋆[Wr(Z)]=KL(P⋆∥Pr).\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{Z\sim P_{\star}}[W_{r}(Z)]=\mathrm{KL}(P_{\star}\|P_{r}).

Also, for the observed dataset Z1,…,ZnZ_{1},\ldots,Z_{n},

1n​∑i=1nWr​(Zi)=ℒ𝒟PrefPref​(r)−ℒ𝒟PrefPref​(r⋆).\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}W_{r}(Z_{i})=\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{Pref}}}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r)-\mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{Pref}}}^{\mathrm{Pref}}(r^{\star}).

Write

Lr≔KL(P⋆∥Pr),L^r≔1n∑i=1nWr(Zi).L_{r}\coloneqq\mathrm{KL}(P_{\star}\|P_{r}),\qquad\widehat{L}_{r}\coloneqq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}W_{r}(Z_{i}).

We now prove concentration of L^r\widehat{L}_{r} around LrL_{r}. The BTL probabilities are uniformly bounded away from 00 and 11 on the return range [0,H][0,H]. Indeed, for all r∈ℛr\in\mathcal{R} and all trajectory pairs,

aC≤Cr​(τ+,τ−)≤1−aC.a_{\mathrm{C}}\leq\mathrm{C}_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-})\leq 1-a_{\mathrm{C}}.

Hence the log-likelihood ratio is bounded:

|Wr​(Z)|≤BC.|W_{r}(Z)|\leq B_{\mathrm{C}}.

We also need the standard self-bounding property of bounded Bernoulli log likelihoods. For p,q∈[aC,1−aC]p,q\in[a_{\mathrm{C}},1-a_{\mathrm{C}}], define

k(p,q)=KL(Bern(p)∥Bern(q))k(p,q)=\mathrm{KL}(\mathrm{Bern}(p)\|\mathrm{Bern}(q))

and

m⁡(p,q)=p​log2​pq+(1−p)​log2​1−p1−q.m(p,q)=p\log^{2}\frac{p}{q}+(1-p)\log^{2}\frac{1-p}{1-q}.

Since the square [aC,1−aC]2[a_{\mathrm{C}},1-a_{\mathrm{C}}]^{2} is compact and m⁡(p,q)/k⁡(p,q)m(p,q)/k(p,q) has a finite continuous extension at p=qp=q, the constant bCb_{\mathrm{C}} in the lemma statement is finite and satisfies m⁡(p,q)≤bC​k​(p,q)m(p,q)\leq b_{\mathrm{C}}k(p,q) for all p,qp,q in this interval.

Applying this pointwise with p=Cr⋆​(τ+,τ−)p=\mathrm{C}_{r^{\star}}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}) and q=Cr​(τ+,τ−)q=\mathrm{C}_{r}(\tau^{+},\tau^{-}), the conditional second moment over the label satisfies

𝔼y|τ+,τ−​[Wr​(Z)2]≤bC​𝔼y|τ+,τ−​[Wr​(Z)].\mathbb{E}_{y\mid\tau^{+},\tau^{-}}[W_{r}(Z)^{2}]\leq b_{\mathrm{C}}\mathbb{E}_{y\mid\tau^{+},\tau^{-}}[W_{r}(Z)].

Taking the outer expectation over (τ+,τ−)∼μ⊗μ(\tau^{+},\tau^{-})\sim\mu\otimes\mu gives

𝔼Z∼P⋆​[Wr​(Z)2]≤bC​𝔼Z∼P⋆​[Wr​(Z)]=bC​Lr.\mathbb{E}_{Z\sim P_{\star}}[W_{r}(Z)^{2}]\leq b_{\mathrm{C}}\mathbb{E}_{Z\sim P_{\star}}[W_{r}(Z)]=b_{\mathrm{C}}L_{r}.

Therefore VarZ∼P⋆​(Wr​(Z))≤bC​Lr\mathrm{Var}_{Z\sim P_{\star}}(W_{r}(Z))\leq b_{\mathrm{C}}L_{r}.

Now apply one-sided Bernstein to the i.i.d. variables Wr​(Z1),…,Wr​(Zn)W_{r}(Z_{1}),\ldots,W_{r}(Z_{n}). Appendix E Lower Bound for Outcome-based Learning

E.1 Proof of Theorem 2: Lower Bound for Sum-Reward Outcomes

We construct a hard family of finite-horizon MDPs with deterministic transitions. Let the horizon be HH, the state space be

𝒮={s1,…,sH},{\mathcal{S}}=\{s_{1},\dots,s_{H}\},

and the action space be 𝒜={0,1}\mathcal{A}=\{0,1\}. The transition kernel is deterministic:

Ph​(sh+1∣sh,a)=1,∀h∈[H−1],a∈𝒜.P_{h}(s_{h+1}\mid s_{h},a)=1,\qquad\forall h\in[H-1],\ a\in\mathcal{A}.

Thus the state is simply the time index, and the only decision is which action to take at each step.

The environments differ only in their reward functions. For a parameter

𝜽=(θ1,…,θH)∈{0,1}H{\bm{\theta}}=(\theta_{1},\dots,\theta_{H})\in\{0,1\}^{H}

and a (to-be-chosen) gap parameter Δ∈[0,1]\Delta\in[0,1], define the reward at step hh by

rh,𝜽(sh,a)=12+Δ2𝟏{a=θh}−Δ2𝟏{a≠θh},a∈{0,1}.r_{h,{\bm{\theta}}}(s_{h},a)=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\Delta}{2}\mathbf{1}\{a=\theta_{h}\}-\frac{\Delta}{2}\mathbf{1}\{a\neq\theta_{h}\},\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.

Equivalently, at each step exactly one action has reward (1+Δ)/2(1+\Delta)/2, and the other has reward (1−Δ)/2(1-\Delta)/2; both lie in [0,1][0,1], so the trajectory return satisfies ∑hrh,𝜽​(sh,ah)∈[0,H]\sum_{h}r_{h,{\bm{\theta}}}(s_{h},a_{h})\in[0,H]. The optimal policy π𝜽⋆\pi_{\bm{\theta}}^{\star} selects action θh\theta_{h} at every step hh, and its value is

J𝜽​(π𝜽⋆)=H2+H​Δ2.J_{\bm{\theta}}(\pi_{\bm{\theta}}^{\star})=\frac{H}{2}+\frac{H\Delta}{2}.

We assume the behavior policy μ\mu chooses the two actions uniformly at every step, so

dhμ​(sh,a)=12.d_{h}^{\mu}(s_{h},a)=\frac{1}{2}.

For any target policy π\pi, we always have dhπ​(sh,a)≤1d_{h}^{\pi}(s_{h},a)\leq 1, therefore

Cs​a=maxπ⁡maxh,s,a​dhπ​(s,a)dhμ​(s,a)≤2.C_{sa}=\max_{\pi}\max_{h,s,a}\frac{d_{h}^{\pi}(s,a)}{d_{h}^{\mu}(s,a)}\leq 2.

Thus Cs​a=2C_{sa}=2 in this construction.

In the outcome-based setting, the learner does not observe stepwise rewards. Instead, for a trajectory

τ=(s1,a1,…,aH,sH),\tau=(s_{1},a_{1},\dots,a_{H},s_{H}),

it only observes a bounded trajectory-level label

Y(τ)∣τ∼H⋅Bernoulli(R𝜽​(τ)H),R𝜽(τ)=∑h=1Hrh,𝜽(sh,ah).Y(\tau)\mid\tau\sim H\cdot\mathrm{Bernoulli}\left(\frac{R_{\bm{\theta}}(\tau)}{H}\right),\qquad R_{\bm{\theta}}(\tau)=\sum_{h=1}^{H}r_{h,{\bm{\theta}}}(s_{h},a_{h}).

Thus Y⁡(τ)∈{0,H}Y(\tau)\in\{0,H\} and 𝔼⁡[Y⁡(τ)∣τ]=R𝜽​(τ)\mathbb{E}[Y(\tau)\mid\tau]=R_{\bm{\theta}}(\tau), matching the bounded unbiased trajectory-outcome model used in the upper bound.

Now identify a trajectory with its action vector

𝐱=(a1,…,aH)∈{0,1}H.\mathbf{x}=(a_{1},\dots,a_{H})\in\{0,1\}^{H}.

Under the uniform behavior policy, 𝐱\mathbf{x} is distributed uniformly over {0,1}H\{0,1\}^{H}. Moreover,

∑h=1Hrh,𝜽(sh,ah)=H2+Δ2∑h=1H(1−2𝟏{ah≠θh})=H2+H​Δ2−Δ∥𝐱−𝜽∥1.\sum_{h=1}^{H}r_{h,{\bm{\theta}}}(s_{h},a_{h})=\frac{H}{2}+\frac{\Delta}{2}\sum_{h=1}^{H}(1-2\mathbf{1}\{a_{h}\neq\theta_{h}\})=\frac{H}{2}+\frac{H\Delta}{2}-\Delta\|\mathbf{x}-{\bm{\theta}}\|_{1}.

Consequently the conditional success probability of the Bernoulli label is

p𝜽​(𝐱)≔ℙ𝜽​(Y=H∣𝐱)=R𝜽​(𝐱)H=12+Δ2−ΔH​‖𝐱−𝜽‖1.p_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x})\coloneqq\mathbb{P}_{\bm{\theta}}(Y=H\mid\mathbf{x})=\frac{R_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x})}{H}=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\Delta}{2}-\frac{\Delta}{H}\|\mathbf{x}-{\bm{\theta}}\|_{1}.

Reduction to a statistical estimation problem

We therefore consider the estimation problem where 𝜽∈Θ⊆{0,1}H{\bm{\theta}}\in\Theta\subseteq\{0,1\}^{H} is unknown and we observe nn i.i.d. samples (𝐱1,Y1),…,(𝐱n,Yn)(\mathbf{x}_{1},Y_{1}),\dots,(\mathbf{x}_{n},Y_{n}) from P𝜽P_{\bm{\theta}}, where

𝐱i∼Unif({0,1}H),Yi∣𝐱i∼H⋅Bernoulli(p𝜽(𝐱i)).\mathbf{x}_{i}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^{H}),\qquad Y_{i}\mid\mathbf{x}_{i}\sim H\cdot\mathrm{Bernoulli}\bigl(p_{\bm{\theta}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\bigr).

An estimator takes

S=(𝐱1,Y1,…,𝐱n,Yn)S=(\mathbf{x}_{1},Y_{1},\dots,\mathbf{x}_{n},Y_{n})

as input and outputs 𝜽^​(S)\widehat{\bm{\theta}}(S). We measure estimation error by

ℓ⁡(𝜽,𝜽^)=Δ​‖𝜽−𝜽^‖1.\ell({\bm{\theta}},\widehat{\bm{\theta}})=\Delta\|{\bm{\theta}}-\widehat{\bm{\theta}}\|_{1}.

Define

ρ⁡(𝜽,𝜽′)=Δ​‖𝜽−𝜽′‖1,Φ⁡(x)=x.\rho({\bm{\theta}},{\bm{\theta}}^{\prime})=\Delta\|{\bm{\theta}}-{\bm{\theta}}^{\prime}\|_{1},\qquad\Phi(x)=x.

By Fano’s inequality, if Θ={𝜽1,…,𝜽M}\Theta=\{{\bm{\theta}}_{1},\dots,{\bm{\theta}}_{M}\} is a δ\delta-packing under ρ\rho, then

ℜ∗:=inf𝜽^sup𝜽∈Θ𝔼⁡[ℓ⁡(𝜽,𝜽^)]≥Φ⁡(δ/2)​(1−1M2∑j,k=1MKL(Pj⊗n∥Pk⊗n)+log2log⁡M).\mathfrak{R}^{*}:=\inf_{\widehat{\bm{\theta}}}\sup_{{\bm{\theta}}\in\Theta}\mathbb{E}[\ell({\bm{\theta}},\widehat{\bm{\theta}})]\geq\Phi(\delta/2)\left(1-\frac{\frac{1}{M^{2}}\sum_{j,k=1}^{M}\mathrm{KL}(P_{j}^{\otimes n}\|P_{k}^{\otimes n})+\log 2}{\log M}\right).

We now bound the KL divergence. Let Pi:=P𝜽iP_{i}:=P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{i}} and Pj:=P𝜽jP_{j}:=P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{j}} denote the single-sample laws. Since the marginal law of 𝐱\mathbf{x} does not depend on 𝜽{\bm{\theta}},

KL(Pi∥Pj)=12H∑𝐱KL(Pi(Y∣𝐱)∥Pj(Y∣𝐱)).\mathrm{KL}(P_{i}\|P_{j})=\frac{1}{2^{H}}\sum_{\mathbf{x}}\mathrm{KL}\big(P_{i}(Y\mid\mathbf{x})\|P_{j}(Y\mid\mathbf{x})\big).

Conditioned on 𝐱\mathbf{x}, both models are Bernoulli labels scaled by HH, and the scaling does not change the KL divergence. Let pi​(𝐱)≔p𝜽i​(𝐱)p_{i}(\mathbf{x})\coloneqq p_{{\bm{\theta}}_{i}}(\mathbf{x}) and pj​(𝐱)≔p𝜽j​(𝐱)p_{j}(\mathbf{x})\coloneqq p_{{\bm{\theta}}_{j}}(\mathbf{x}). If Δ≤1/2\Delta\leq 1/2, then pi​(𝐱),pj​(𝐱)∈[1/4,3/4]p_{i}(\mathbf{x}),p_{j}(\mathbf{x})\in[1/4,3/4] for every 𝐱\mathbf{x}, and the standard Bernoulli KL bound gives

KL(Pi(Y∣𝐱)∥Pj(Y∣𝐱))=KL(Bern(pi(𝐱))∥Bern(pj(𝐱)))≤8(pi(𝐱)−pj(𝐱))2.\mathrm{KL}\big(P_{i}(Y\mid\mathbf{x})\|P_{j}(Y\mid\mathbf{x})\big)=\mathrm{KL}\big(\mathrm{Bern}(p_{i}(\mathbf{x}))\|\mathrm{Bern}(p_{j}(\mathbf{x}))\big)\leq 8\bigl(p_{i}(\mathbf{x})-p_{j}(\mathbf{x})\bigr)^{2}.

Moreover,

pi​(𝐱)−pj​(𝐱)=−ΔH​(‖𝐱−𝜽i‖1−‖𝐱−𝜽j‖1).p_{i}(\mathbf{x})-p_{j}(\mathbf{x})=-\frac{\Delta}{H}\Big(\|\mathbf{x}-{\bm{\theta}}_{i}\|_{1}-\|\mathbf{x}-{\bm{\theta}}_{j}\|_{1}\Big).

Thus

KL(Pi∥Pj)≤8​Δ2H2⋅12H∑𝐱(∥𝐱−𝜽i∥1−∥𝐱−𝜽j∥1)2.\mathrm{KL}(P_{i}\|P_{j})\leq\frac{8\Delta^{2}}{H^{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{2^{H}}\sum_{\mathbf{x}}\Big(\|\mathbf{x}-{\bm{\theta}}_{i}\|_{1}-\|\mathbf{x}-{\bm{\theta}}_{j}\|_{1}\Big)^{2}.

Now let

ℐ:={h∈[H]:θi,h≠θj,h},|ℐ|=‖𝜽i−𝜽j‖1.\mathcal{I}:=\{h\in[H]:\theta_{i,h}\neq\theta_{j,h}\},\qquad|\mathcal{I}|=\|{\bm{\theta}}_{i}-{\bm{\theta}}_{j}\|_{1}.

Comparing the two Hamming distances coordinate by coordinate, only coordinates in ℐ\mathcal{I} contribute. For each h∈ℐh\in\mathcal{I}, the difference |xh−θi,h|−|xh−θj,h||x_{h}-\theta_{i,h}|-|x_{h}-\theta_{j,h}| has mean zero and square one under xh∼Unif​{0,1}x_{h}\sim\mathrm{Unif}\{0,1\}, and the coordinate contributions are independent. Therefore,

12H​∑𝐱(‖𝐱−𝜽i‖1−‖𝐱−𝜽j‖1)2=𝔼𝐱​(‖𝐱−𝜽i‖1−‖𝐱−𝜽j‖1)2=|ℐ|=‖𝜽i−𝜽j‖1.\frac{1}{2^{H}}\sum_{\mathbf{x}}\Big(\|\mathbf{x}-{\bm{\theta}}_{i}\|_{1}-\|\mathbf{x}-{\bm{\theta}}_{j}\|_{1}\Big)^{2}=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}}\Big(\|\mathbf{x}-{\bm{\theta}}_{i}\|_{1}-\|\mathbf{x}-{\bm{\theta}}_{j}\|_{1}\Big)^{2}=|\mathcal{I}|=\|{\bm{\theta}}_{i}-{\bm{\theta}}_{j}\|_{1}.

It follows that

KL(Pi∥Pj)≤8​Δ2H2∥𝜽i−𝜽j∥1.\mathrm{KL}(P_{i}\|P_{j})\leq\frac{8\Delta^{2}}{H^{2}}\|{\bm{\theta}}_{i}-{\bm{\theta}}_{j}\|_{1}.

Since the samples are i.i.d.,

KL(Pi⊗n∥Pj⊗n)=nKL(Pi∥Pj)≤8​n​Δ2H2∥𝜽i−𝜽j∥1.\mathrm{KL}(P_{i}^{\otimes n}\|P_{j}^{\otimes n})=n\mathrm{KL}(P_{i}\|P_{j})\leq\frac{8n\Delta^{2}}{H^{2}}\|{\bm{\theta}}_{i}-{\bm{\theta}}_{j}\|_{1}.

Next, by the Varshamov–Gilbert lemma, there exists a subset

Θ={𝜽1,…,𝜽M}⊆{0,1}H\Theta=\{{\bm{\theta}}_{1},\dots,{\bm{\theta}}_{M}\}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{H}

such that

log⁡M≥H8,‖𝜽i−𝜽j‖1≥H8,∀i≠j.\log M\geq\frac{H}{8},\qquad\|{\bm{\theta}}_{i}-{\bm{\theta}}_{j}\|_{1}\geq\frac{H}{8},\quad\forall i\neq j.

Hence Θ\Theta is a δ\delta-packing under ρ\rho with

δ=mini≠j⁡ρ⁡(𝜽i,𝜽j)≥Δ​H8.\delta=\min_{i\neq j}\rho({\bm{\theta}}_{i},{\bm{\theta}}_{j})\geq\frac{\Delta H}{8}.

Also, since ‖𝜽i−𝜽j‖1≤H\|{\bm{\theta}}_{i}-{\bm{\theta}}_{j}\|_{1}\leq H,

maxi≠jKL(Pi⊗n∥Pj⊗n)≤8​n​Δ2H.\max_{i\neq j}\mathrm{KL}(P_{i}^{\otimes n}\|P_{j}^{\otimes n})\leq\frac{8n\Delta^{2}}{H}.

Choose

Δ=H16​n,\Delta=\frac{H}{16\sqrt{n}},

which is feasible with Δ≤1/2\Delta\leq 1/2 under the theorem’s standing condition n≥64​H2n\geq 64H^{2}. Then

maxi≠jKL(Pi⊗n∥Pj⊗n)≤H32.\max_{i\neq j}\mathrm{KL}(P_{i}^{\otimes n}\|P_{j}^{\otimes n})\leq\frac{H}{32}.

Since log⁡M≥H/8\log M\geq H/8, we have

maxi≠jKL(Pi⊗n∥Pj⊗n)≤14logM.\max_{i\neq j}\mathrm{KL}(P_{i}^{\otimes n}\|P_{j}^{\otimes n})\leq\frac{1}{4}\log M.

Moreover, choose the universal constant H0H_{0} in Theorem 2 large enough that exp⁡(H0/8)≥16\exp(H_{0}/8)\geq 16. Then H≥H0H\geq H_{0} and log⁡M≥H/8\log M\geq H/8 imply M≥16M\geq 16, hence log⁡M≥4​log⁡2\log M\geq 4\log 2. Therefore Fano’s inequality (Yu, 1997) gives

ℜ∗≥Φ⁡(δ/2)​(1−14​log⁡M+log⁡2log⁡M)≥12​Φ​(δ/2)=δ4≥Δ​H32.\mathfrak{R}^{*}\geq\Phi(\delta/2)\left(1-\frac{\frac{1}{4}\log M+\log 2}{\log M}\right)\geq\frac{1}{2}\Phi(\delta/2)=\frac{\delta}{4}\geq\frac{\Delta H}{32}.

Substituting the choice of Δ\Delta yields

ℜ∗≥H2512​n.\mathfrak{R}^{*}\geq\frac{H^{2}}{512\sqrt{n}}.

Return to the original lower bound for outcome-based RL

Finally, we translate this estimation lower bound back to policy learning. Given an output policy π^\widehat{\pi}, define an estimator 𝜽^​(π^)\widehat{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi}) by choosing, at each stage, an action with maximal probability under π^h(⋅∣sh)\widehat{\pi}_{h}(\cdot\mid s_{h}), breaking ties arbitrarily. If θ^h≠θh\widehat{\theta}_{h}\neq\theta_{h}, then π^\widehat{\pi} puts probability at most 1/21/2 on the optimal action at stage hh, and hence loses at least Δ/2\Delta/2 in expected reward at that stage. Therefore,

J𝜽​(π𝜽⋆)−J𝜽​(π^)≥Δ2​‖𝜽−𝜽^​(π^)‖1.J_{\bm{\theta}}(\pi_{\bm{\theta}}^{\star})-J_{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi})\geq\frac{\Delta}{2}\|{\bm{\theta}}-\widehat{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi})\|_{1}.

Hence

infπ^sup𝜽𝔼⁡[J𝜽​(π𝜽⋆)−J𝜽​(π^)]≥12​ℜ∗≥H21024​n.\inf_{\widehat{\pi}}\sup_{{\bm{\theta}}}\mathbb{E}\big[J_{\bm{\theta}}(\pi_{\bm{\theta}}^{\star})-J_{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi})\big]\geq\frac{1}{2}\mathfrak{R}^{*}\geq\frac{H^{2}}{1024\sqrt{n}}.

Equivalently, to guarantee suboptimality at most ε\varepsilon, one must have

ε≥H21024​n,that is,n≥H410242​ε2.\varepsilon\geq\frac{H^{2}}{1024\sqrt{n}},\qquad\text{that is,}\qquad n\geq\frac{H^{4}}{1024^{2}\varepsilon^{2}}.

Since Cs​a=2C_{sa}=2 in this construction, this can be written in the standard form

n=Ω⁡(H4​Cs​aε2).n=\Omega\left(\frac{H^{4}C_{sa}}{\varepsilon^{2}}\right).

E.2 Proof of Theorem 5: Exponential Lower Bound for All-Success Aggregation

We prove the lower bound for the all-success outcome described in Example 4. We construct a hard family of deterministic finite-horizon MDPs with binary rewards. Let the horizon be HH, the state space be

𝒮={s1,…,sH},{\mathcal{S}}=\{s_{1},\dots,s_{H}\},

and the action space be 𝒜={0,1}\mathcal{A}=\{0,1\}. The transition kernel is deterministic:

Ph​(sh+1∣sh,a)=1,∀h∈[H−1],a∈𝒜.P_{h}(s_{h+1}\mid s_{h},a)=1,\qquad\forall h\in[H-1],\ a\in\mathcal{A}.

Thus the state is again only the time index, and the learner chooses one binary action at each step.

The environments differ only in their reward functions. For a parameter

𝜽=(θ1,…,θH)∈{0,1}H,{\bm{\theta}}=(\theta_{1},\dots,\theta_{H})\in\{0,1\}^{H},

define the binary reward at step hh by

rh,𝜽(sh,a)=𝟏{a=θh}∈{0,1},\addcontentsline{lla}{section}{\numberline q:lb-allsuccess-rewards}r_{h,{\bm{\theta}}}(s_{h},a)=\mathbf{1}\{a=\theta_{h}\}\in\{0,1\}, (72)

and define the observed outcome using the all-success aggregation of Example 4:

Y(τ)=R𝜽(τ)=∏h=1Hrh,𝜽(sh,ah)=𝟏{ah=θh∀h}.Y(\tau)=R_{\bm{\theta}}(\tau)=\prod_{h=1}^{H}r_{h,{\bm{\theta}}}(s_{h},a_{h})=\mathbf{1}\{a_{h}=\theta_{h}\ \forall h\}.

The optimal policy π𝜽⋆\pi_{\bm{\theta}}^{\star} selects action θh\theta_{h} at every step, and therefore

J𝜽​(π𝜽⋆)=1.J_{\bm{\theta}}(\pi_{\bm{\theta}}^{\star})=1.

We assume the behavior policy μ\mu chooses the two actions uniformly at every step. Identifying a trajectory with its action vector

𝐱=(a1,…,aH)∈{0,1}H,\mathbf{x}=(a_{1},\dots,a_{H})\in\{0,1\}^{H},

we have 𝐱∼Unif⁡({0,1}H)\mathbf{x}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^{H}) and the observed label is

y=𝟏{𝐱=𝜽}.y=\mathbf{1}\{\mathbf{x}={\bm{\theta}}\}.

Coverage

Since μ\mu is uniform,

dhμ​(sh,a)=12.d_{h}^{\mu}(s_{h},a)=\frac{1}{2}.

For the optimal policy, dhπ𝜽⋆​(sh,θh)=1d_{h}^{\pi^{\star}_{\bm{\theta}}}(s_{h},\theta_{h})=1, and hence

Cs​a​(π𝜽⋆)=maxh,s,a⁡dhπ𝜽⋆​(s,a)dhμ​(s,a)=2.C_{sa}(\pi^{\star}_{\bm{\theta}})=\max_{h,s,a}\frac{d_{h}^{\pi^{\star}_{\bm{\theta}}}(s,a)}{d_{h}^{\mu}(s,a)}=2.

At the trajectory level, however, μ⁡(τ)=2−H\mu(\tau)=2^{-H} for every trajectory, while π𝜽⋆\pi^{\star}_{\bm{\theta}} puts all its mass on the single trajectory 𝐱=𝜽\mathbf{x}={\bm{\theta}}. Thus

Cτ​(π𝜽⋆)≔maxτ⁡ℙπ𝜽⋆​[τ]ℙμ​[τ]=2H.C_{\tau}(\pi^{\star}_{\bm{\theta}})\coloneqq\max_{\tau}\frac{\mathbb{P}_{\pi^{\star}_{\bm{\theta}}}[\tau]}{\mathbb{P}_{\mu}[\tau]}=2^{H}.

The construction therefore has constant state–action concentrability but exponential trajectory concentrability.

Reduction to parameter estimation

For any possibly randomized policy π^\widehat{\pi} and any 𝜽∈{0,1}H{\bm{\theta}}\in\{0,1\}^{H}, the deterministic-chain structure gives

J𝜽​(π^)=𝔼π^​[R𝜽​(τ)]=∏h=1Hℙπ^​[ah=θh∣sh],J𝜽​(π𝜽⋆)=1.\addcontentsline{lla}{section}{\numberline q:lb-allsuccess-valgap}J_{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi})=\mathbb{E}_{\widehat{\pi}}[R_{\bm{\theta}}(\tau)]=\prod_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{P}_{\widehat{\pi}}[a_{h}=\theta_{h}\mid s_{h}],\qquad J_{\bm{\theta}}(\pi^{\star}_{\bm{\theta}})=1. (73)

Given π^\widehat{\pi}, define an induced estimator 𝜽^​(π^)\widehat{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi}) by choosing the most likely action at every step, breaking ties arbitrarily:

θ^h​(π^)≔arg⁡maxa∈{0,1}​π^h​(a∣sh)∈{0,1},𝜽^​(π^)≔(θ^1,…,θ^H).\addcontentsline{lla}{section}{\numberline q:lb-allsuccess-argmax}\widehat{\theta}_{h}(\widehat{\pi})\coloneqq\arg\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\widehat{\pi}_{h}(a\mid s_{h})\in\{0,1\},\qquad\widehat{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi})\coloneqq(\widehat{\theta}_{1},\dots,\widehat{\theta}_{H}). (74)

The following lemma converts value suboptimality into zero-one parameter-estimation loss.

Lemma 19 (Reduction from value gap to zero-one loss).

For every policy π^\widehat{\pi} and every 𝛉∈{0,1}H{\bm{\theta}}\in\{0,1\}^{H},

J𝜽(π𝜽⋆)−J𝜽(π^)≥12𝟏{𝜽^(π^)≠𝜽}.J_{\bm{\theta}}(\pi^{\star}_{\bm{\theta}})-J_{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi})\geq\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{1}\bigl\{\widehat{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi})\neq{\bm{\theta}}\bigr\}.
Proof.

If 𝜽^​(π^)=𝜽\widehat{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi})={\bm{\theta}}, the right-hand side is zero and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, there exists h⋆∈[H]h^{\star}\in[H] such that θ^h⋆≠θh⋆\widehat{\theta}_{h^{\star}}\neq\theta_{h^{\star}}. By Eq. 74,

π^h⋆​(θh⋆∣sh⋆)≤12.\widehat{\pi}_{h^{\star}}(\theta_{h^{\star}}\mid s_{h^{\star}})\leq\frac{1}{2}.

Using Eq. 73 and the bound π^h​(θh∣sh)≤1\widehat{\pi}_{h}(\theta_{h}\mid s_{h})\leq 1 for all h≠h⋆h\neq h^{\star},

J𝜽​(π^)=∏h=1Hπ^h​(θh∣sh)≤π^h⋆​(θh⋆∣sh⋆)≤12,J_{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi})=\prod_{h=1}^{H}\widehat{\pi}_{h}(\theta_{h}\mid s_{h})\leq\widehat{\pi}_{h^{\star}}(\theta_{h^{\star}}\mid s_{h^{\star}})\leq\frac{1}{2},

so J𝜽​(π𝜽⋆)−J𝜽​(π^)≥1−1/2=1/2J_{\bm{\theta}}(\pi^{\star}_{\bm{\theta}})-J_{\bm{\theta}}(\widehat{\pi})\geq 1-1/2=1/2. ∎

Indistinguishability via total variation

Let P𝜽P_{\bm{\theta}} be the law of one sample (𝐱,y)(\mathbf{x},y), where 𝐱∼Unif⁡({0,1}H)\mathbf{x}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^{H}) and y=𝟏{𝐱=𝜽}y=\mathbf{1}\{\mathbf{x}={\bm{\theta}}\}. Let P𝜽⊗nP_{\bm{\theta}}^{\otimes n} denote the law of nn i.i.d. samples. We now bound the total variation distance between the observation laws corresponding to two distinct parameters.

Lemma 20 (Trajectory-coverage TV bound).

For any distinct 𝛉0,𝛉1∈{0,1}H{\bm{\theta}}_{0},{\bm{\theta}}_{1}\in\{0,1\}^{H},

TV⁡(P𝜽0,P𝜽1)=21−H,TV⁡(P𝜽0⊗n,P𝜽1⊗n)≤n⋅21−H.\mathrm{TV}(P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{0}},P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{1}})=2^{1-H},\qquad\mathrm{TV}(P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{0}}^{\otimes n},P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{1}}^{\otimes n})\leq n\cdot 2^{1-H}.
Proof.

Under both P𝜽0P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{0}} and P𝜽1P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{1}}, the marginal distribution of 𝐱\mathbf{x} is uniform. If 𝐱∉{𝜽0,𝜽1}\mathbf{x}\notin\{{\bm{\theta}}_{0},{\bm{\theta}}_{1}\}, then y=0y=0 under both laws. If 𝐱=𝜽0\mathbf{x}={\bm{\theta}}_{0}, then y=1y=1 under P𝜽0P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{0}} and y=0y=0 under P𝜽1P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{1}}; the case 𝐱=𝜽1\mathbf{x}={\bm{\theta}}_{1} is symmetric. Therefore

TV⁡(P𝜽0,P𝜽1)=12​∑𝐱,y|P𝜽0​(𝐱,y)−P𝜽1​(𝐱,y)|=12⋅2⋅(2−H+2−H)=21−H.\mathrm{TV}(P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{0}},P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{1}})=\frac{1}{2}\ \sum_{\mathbf{x},y}\bigl|P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{0}}(\mathbf{x},y)-P_{{\bm{\theta}}_{1}}(\mathbf{x},y)\bigr|=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot\bigl(2^{-H}+2^{-H}\bigr)=2^{1-H}.

For the nn-sample bound, couple the two experiments by drawing

𝐱1,…,𝐱n∼i.i.d.Unif({0,1}H),yi(b)≔𝟏{𝐱i=𝜽b},b∈{0,1}.\mathbf{x}_{1},\dots,\mathbf{x}_{n}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{i.i.d.}}}{{\sim}}\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^{H}),\qquad y_{i}^{(b)}\coloneqq\mathbf{1}\{\mathbf{x}_{i}={\bm{\theta}}_{b}\},\quad b\in\{0,1\}.

Under this coupling,

X(b)≔(𝐱1,y1(b),…,𝐱n,yn(b))X^{(b)}\coloneqq(\mathbf{x}_{1},y_{1}^{(b)},\dots,\mathbf{x}_{n},y_{n}^{(b)})

has marginal law P𝜽b⊗nP_{{\bm{\theta}}_{b}}^{\otimes n} for each b∈{0,1}b\in\{0,1\}. Define

E≔{𝐱i∉{𝜽0,𝜽1}
